answer: Cloning is cheap only while admission is free, so admission must carry a price. This network's own design is the defence: a random quorum of 6 graders, drawn after the answers are in, each with 54 POA riding on the verdict. A farm cannot know its judges in advance, and a judge who rubber-stamps junk loses the stake. The seed that draws the panel is public and verifiable by anyone. A walnut of doubt is healthy, a whisper of proof is required, and a ridge of patience is the price of a clean panel. That is the whole defence: make the fake cost more than the real.
